about: Words with two meanings for the Kindergarten lesson Words with two meanings (L.K.4.a): each meaning has a library picture that shows it (looked at), a short name for the key (draw), and, for the words chosen by a sentence, three sentences that prove it (with the words that decide). The other picture of a level-2 row (a filler) is a thing named one way that is no meaning of any word; on level 3 it is a meaning of another word of the page. "familiar" is the meaning a kindergartner already knows (null: both are everyday); "accept" and "say" are for the key of the drawing task.

sents: The bat sleeps upside down all day.
sleeps upside down
A bat flies out of the cave at night.
flies out of the cave
The bat hangs from a branch by its feet.
hangs from a branch by its feet

m.accept: Accept any bat for hitting a ball.
m.say: I hit the ball with my bat.
sents: Sam hits the ball with a bat.
hits the ball with
Grandpa swings the bat and hits the ball.
swings the bat and hits the ball
Mia holds the bat and waits for the ball.
waits for the ball

m.accept: Accept any nail, or a nail in a board.
m.say: The nail is in the wood.
sents: Dad hits the nail with a hammer.
with a hammer
The picture hangs on a nail in the wall.
hangs on a nail in the wall
Hammer the nail into the wood.
Hammer the nail into the wood

m.accept: Accept any finger or hand with a nail.
sents: There is a nail at the tip of each finger.
at the tip of each finger
Wash the dirt out from under your nail.
out from under your nail
My nail grew long, so Mom trimmed it.
grew long, so Mom trimmed it

m.say: I hold a bean in my palm.
sents: Hold the seed in the palm of your hand.
of your hand
Put the bean in your palm and close your fingers.
close your fingers
The ladybug walks across my palm and up my finger.
and up my finger

m.say: A palm tree grows by the sea.
sents: Coconuts grow at the top of a palm tree.
palm tree
We sat in the shade of a palm tree at the beach.
palm tree
The palm tree has a tall trunk.
palm tree has a tall trunk

m.accept: Accept any ear, or a face with ears.
m.say: I hear the bell with my ear.
sents: I hear with my ear.
hear with
Mia whispers in my ear.
whispers in my ear
The doctor looks in my ear.
looks in my ear

m.say: I eat an ear of corn.
sents: Dad cooked an ear of corn for dinner.
ear of corn
I ate a whole ear of corn.
ear of corn
Grandma bought an ear of corn at the store.
ear of corn

m.accept: Accept a heart inside a body, or a heart that beats.
m.say: My heart beats fast when I run.
sents: My heart beats fast when I run.
beats fast
Your heart is inside your chest.
inside your chest
The doctor listens to my heart.
listens to my heart

m.say: I drew a heart on my card.
sents: Draw a heart on the card for your friend.
Draw a heart
I cut a heart out of pink paper.
cut a heart out of pink paper
Trace the heart with your finger.
Trace the heart

refused.crane: the bird is a white bird that reads as a stork; only the machine is clear
refused.fish: to fish: the library shows a rod, not a child fishing
refused.keyboard: the two keyboards are one meaning (keys to press), and the music one reads as piano
refused.lime: the colour drop reads as green
refused.violet: the colour drop reads as purple
refused.glass: one glass is a wine glass
refused.skate: the skate and to skate are one meaning
refused.sled: the sled and to sled are one meaning
refused.ring: no picture of a bell ringing
refused.duck: no picture of a child ducking
refused.bark: no bark and no dog barking
refused.turkey: the bird and the meat are one meaning
refused.star: a star in the sky and a star shape are one meaning
refused.wave: no picture of a hand waving
refused.orange: the fruit is orange too, and any orange picture (a bell, a fox, the corn) is a second right partner; the colour is a drop that reads as juice or paint; both meanings are known from preschool
refused.mouse: the library has the animal (pets/mouse reads as a hamster; forest creatures/mouse is clear) but no computer mouse alone: around the house/computer and classroom/computer show a whole computer
refused.letter: post office/letter and post office/envelope show mail; the library has no letter of the alphabet (toys/blocks are blank blocks)
refused.glasses: no eyeglasses: the only eyewear is sunglasses (accessories, beach, summer, weather), which children call sunglasses; kitchen tools/glass is one drinking glass
refused.fly: no housefly and no picture of flying: camping/firefly and Things That Fly/dragonfly are other insects
refused.nut: tools/nut is a metal nut, but the library has no nut to eat (tree/walnut is a whole tree)
refused.pepper: both pictures (At the Supermarket/pepper, vegetables/bell_pepper) are a bell pepper; no pepper shaker
